# realuptime_status_page_component (Resource)

Publishes one of the account's checks on a status page as a public component (`POST /status-pages/{id}/components`). The check keeps running when the component is destroyed; only its public listing goes. A check can appear once per page (RU-5012). Agent-bound monitors are refused: they are private by design (RU-5008). Import with `<status_page_id>/<component_id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Publish the API check on the status page under a public label.
resource "realuptime_status_page_component" "api" {
  status_page_id = realuptime_status_page.public.id
  check_id       = realuptime_check.api.id
  display_name   = "API"
  description    = "REST API and webhooks"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by internal/docsgen -->
## Schema

### Required

- `check_id` (String) The check to publish. Changing it replaces the component.
- `status_page_id` (String) The page to publish on. Changing it replaces the component (use the dashboard's move to keep subscribers).

### Optional

- `description` (String) Tooltip text on the public page, at most 200 characters. Null renders no tooltip.
- `display_name` (String) Public label on the status page, 1-200 characters. Defaults to the check's name at creation and is independent of it afterwards (renaming the check does not rename the component, or the reverse).

### Read-Only

- `group_id` (String) Display group, if the component was grouped from the dashboard (read-only here).
- `id` (String) Component id (UUID).
- `sort_order` (Number) Position on the page (appended at creation; reordered from the dashboard).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import with "<status_page_id>/<component_id>".
terraform import realuptime_status_page_component.api 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222/33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333
```
